findings.location: Design Notes > Worker interface ("Parseable = a JSON object with those keys and engine = the worker's, whatever the exit code" vs "a worker that exits 143 or by a signal while the version process was not stopped is a crash")
findings.issue: These two rules conflict when a worker has already written a valid result file and then exits 143 or by a signal while the version process was not stopped. Examples: SIGKILL from the OOM killer during Playwright/interpreter shutdown, a SIGTERM that lands after `os.replace`, or a stray signal. The first rule says to use the result. The second says the cell is `crash`. Neither rule says which one wins.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer has to pick an order: check the exit code first, or check that the result parses first. One order turns a fully driven cell (possibly a `fail` with conclusive findings) into `inconclusive` `crash`, which hides a blocking failure and feeds Plan step 3 `blocked-infra`. The other order keeps it. The unit tests for the Worker crash row will then encode whichever order was picked.
findings.suggestion: State the precedence explicitly. For example: a parseable result always wins, whatever the exit code or signal. The 143/signal rule applies only when no parseable result exists, and decides only whether the cell is `crash` or skipped under the stop path. Add a unit case: result written, then exit -9.

findings.location: Design Notes > Worker interface (spec.json carries both `ctx` and a top-level `screenshot_dir`); Always > Child (screenshots in `<shots>/<ver>/<engine>`)
findings.issue: Today's version `ctx` already contains `screenshot_dir` = `<shots>/<ver>` (ps-e2e-run.py `_run_one_version_inner`), and `_snap` reads `ctx['screenshot_dir']`. spec.json serialises that `ctx` and also has a separate top-level `screenshot_dir` (`<shots>/<ver>/<engine>`). The spec doesn't say the worker must overwrite `ctx['screenshot_dir']` with the top-level value. It also doesn't say what the worker does when the best-effort mkdir of `<ver>/<engine>` failed: null, or fall back to `<ver>`.
findings.implementation_impact: If the worker passes `ctx` through unchanged, parallel screenshots land flat in `<ver>/`. Both engines then write into one folder, contradicting the contract's per-engine subdir and the rewritten SKILL.md/quickstart paths. Visual review would then look in `<ver>/<engine>/` and find nothing.
findings.suggestion: Either drop `screenshot_dir` from the serialised `ctx` and keep only the top-level key, or state that the worker sets `ctx['screenshot_dir']` from the top-level key, which is null when the version process failed to create the subdir (screenshots skipped, as today).

findings.location: Code Map / Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py (`progress_attach(path, version)`); Design Notes > Worker interface (spec.json `slow_after`, worker registers under the Job ID)
findings.issue: spec.json carries `slow_after`, but the specified helper `fl.progress_attach(path, version)` has no parameter for it. `progress_init` is forbidden in workers, and `phase._beat` reads `_PROGRESS['slow_after']`. The spec also leaves the order of `progress_attach` and `job_register` open. `job_register` snapshots `_PROGRESS['path']` into the registry entry (`progress_file`) at registration time, and needs `module`/`layer`/`versions`, which spec.json does not carry by name.
findings.implementation_impact: A literal implementation silently ignores the operator's `--slow-after` in workers, so `browser:<engine>`, the longest phase, uses the 180 s default. Registering before attaching leaves `progress_file: null` in the workers' registry entries, which `--list-jobs` shows. The implementer also has to guess the module name for `job_register`, for example from `ctx['mod']`.
findings.suggestion: Specify `progress_attach(path, version, slow_after)`, or say that it also sets `_PROGRESS['slow_after']`. State the worker start order (set `fl.RUN_ID`, `progress_attach`, `job_register(job_id, module=ctx['mod'], layer='e2e', versions=version)`, `timing_activate`), or add `module` to spec.json.

findings.location: Always > Child, bullet 2 (`LOCK_EX` when the scenario 'has a BO `goto`', else `LOCK_SH`); contract Cross-engine lock (`_needs_bo` per scenario)
findings.issue: BO is detected only by `goto` with `area: "bo"`. `_resolve_url` also accepts `url` (for example `{bo}/index.php?controller=AdminOrders`) with no area, and `discover_scenarios` accepts such specs without a note. A spec that reaches the back office through `url` is classed FO-only, so it takes `LOCK_SH` and runs on both engines at once against BO state.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer builds exactly what is written. On such a module, the headline guarantee ('a BO scenario can never overlap, and so never mask, another engine's scenario') is silently false, and live test (c) cannot catch it because its BO-scenario set uses the same classifier. Masked failures then pass unless a finding triggers a rerun.
findings.suggestion: Either classify a scenario as BO when any `goto` resolves under `ctx['bo']` (the area or a `url` beginning with `{bo}`/the admin path), or have `discover_scenarios` emit a scenario note for a `url` goto into the admin path with no `area: bo`, so such a spec drops `ready` instead of silently weakening the lock. If this changes the contract, it is Ask First.

findings.location: Code Map (`_drive_page`/`drive_engine` -- per-scenario hook, spans); Design Notes > `scenario_spans` (worker: lock + spans + marker; in-process first pass: spans only; sequential passes: none)
findings.issue: `drive_engine` and `_drive_page` must behave three ways depending on the pass. Worker passes take the lock, hold the holder marker, record spans and write step markers. The in-process first pass (single engine or sequential fallback) records spans only. `rerun-seq` and BO-login fallback passes do none of these. The spec names no seam for selecting the mode (a new parameter, a hook object, or a ctx key). `ctx` is serialised into spec.json and copied per scenario.
findings.implementation_impact: Putting the mode in `ctx` leaks it into spec.json and the per-scenario `local` dicts, and invites in-process passes to inherit a worker flag. Forgetting to disable spans in sequential passes lets the rerun overwrite the lockstep `scenario_spans`, which the merge rule and live test (c) rely on. The stub tests ("lock and barrier with real flock/files across threads") also need a seam to inject.
findings.suggestion: Name the seam. For example, `drive_engine(engine, scenarios, ctx, headed=False, hook=None)`, where `hook` is an object with `before(k, scenario)` and `after(k, scenario)`. The worker passes a LockstepHook, the in-process first pass a SpanHook, and sequential passes None. Spans are returned in the result and never stored in `ctx`.

findings.location: Tasks > ps-e2e-run.py ('worker timings re-recorded into the version sink in order so suffixes continue'); Design Notes > Phases (`browser:<engine>#2` for the BO-login fallback); I/O row BO-login fallback
findings.issue: The spec says worker timings are re-recorded into the version sink, but not when relative to the sequential passes. Suffixes are assigned by order of `TimingSink.record` calls. The worker's lockstep `browser:firefox` must therefore be recorded before the fallback pass's `browser:firefox` for the fallback to become `#2`. Likewise, the worker's `lock-wait`/`barrier-wait` entries must be recorded before any in-process phase of the same engine.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer who collects worker results at reap time but re-records timings while assembling cells at the end (after the confirmation passes) gets the fallback as bare `browser:firefox` and the discarded lockstep pass as `browser:firefox#2`. This inverts which duration the I/O row and docs call the counting pass. `_engine_failed`-style mid-run reads of the sink would also see no lockstep phase.
findings.suggestion: State that each worker's timings are re-recorded when that worker is reaped (or all of them right after the last reap), and always before the first sequential pass.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:90 (Design Notes > Confirmation merge, BO-login fallback)
findings.issue: The BO-login fallback pass cannot launch (launch_error), or fails after launch. Its first pass was already discarded, and only the parallel-unconfirmed path says where the discarded first-pass findings go (parallel_only). Here the merge says findings and inconclusive are 'that pass's alone'.
findings.implementation_impact: Conclusive FO findings from the discarded lockstep pass disappear without a trace. The cell reads inconclusive launch-error with empty findings and parallel_only, which breaks the honesty law ('unconfirmable findings never pass silently').
findings.suggestion: State that when the fallback pass returns launch_error, the discarded first pass's findings move to parallel_only (as in the parallel-unconfirmed rule), and its findings are [].

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:90 (Confirmation merge field list) / :91 (Worker interface)
findings.issue: The merge names which pass supplies each cell field, but browser_notes is not listed. Today the version loop's note() writes the 'browser X gagal diluncurkan' note. The spec does not say whether the version process writes this note for a worker's launch_error, or for a rerun or fallback pass that cannot launch.
findings.implementation_impact: A launch-error cell may carry no explanatory browser_notes entry, or the version-level legacy browser_notes may differ by implementation. Operators lose the remediation hint, and unit tests cannot pin the expected notes.
findings.suggestion: Add browser_notes to the merge: the first pass's notes plus a launch-error note (same text as today) for each pass whose launch_error is set. The version process writes it for worker results too.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27 (Always > Child, psm.slots stamping)
findings.issue: A direct run passes an explicit --slot-cost lower than n (e.g. --slot-cost 1) with two probed engines and no --sequential-browsers. The child runs in parallel mode and stamps psm.slots=1. Only the no-flag case (stamp n) is defined.
findings.implementation_impact: The daemon-wide slot count under-reports a parallel boot. Concurrent ps-run-layer admissions over-subscribe the host by one browser per such run.
findings.suggestion: Specify one: reject --slot-cost < n in parallel mode (exit 2), force parallel mode off (behave as --sequential-browsers), or stamp max(--slot-cost, n).

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27, :89 ('in psm_e2e_browsers order')
findings.issue: The confirmation-pass order and the sequential-fallback order are defined as psm_e2e_browsers order. The child gets its engine set from --engines (runner) or --browsers (direct run), possibly in a different order, and may have no --config at all.
findings.implementation_impact: The order of sequential passes and of the sequential fallback depends on the code path. It decides which engine gets not-run after fail-fast and which engine becomes parallel-unconfirmed after a reset failure, so the same inputs can yield different records.
findings.suggestion: Define the order source: psm_e2e_browsers from --config when present, filtered to the driven engines; otherwise the --engines/--browsers order. Have the runner pass --engines in config order.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:93 (reset-opcache master detection)
findings.issue: The set -e script reads /proc/<pid>/comm for every process and its parent. A php-fpm worker can exit between the /proc scan and the read (pm dynamic/ondemand), or a parent can be pid 0. The spec does not say how a vanished or unreadable /proc entry is handled.
findings.implementation_impact: A routine race aborts the set -e script before the sentinel, so reset-opcache fails spuriously. Every later engine needing a pass gets parallel-unconfirmed, or sequential-reset in the fallback, and the next run is forced to cost 1.
findings.suggestion: Specify that unreadable or vanished /proc entries are skipped, e.g. c=$(cat /proc/$p/comm 2>/dev/null) || continue, and that only the final count of masters (exactly one) decides failure.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:93 (reset-opcache success = sentinel after kill -USR2)
findings.issue: kill -USR2 only signals the php-fpm master; the reload (re-exec, children respawned) completes asynchronously after the sentinel is printed. Nothing defines waiting for the reload to finish.
findings.implementation_impact: wait-http can succeed against pre-reload children, so the rerun's first request may hit the reload window (502 or reset connection). A rerun failure always blocks, so this becomes a false blocking finding.
findings.suggestion: Require reset-opcache to wait until the master pid serves again, e.g. poll until new child pids exist (children whose ppid is the master and whose start time is after the kill), with a bound under --timeout, before echoing PSM_RESET_OPCACHE_OK.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:93 (docroot listing under set -e)
findings.issue: The find listing runs in a set -e script. A file that vanishes during traversal (log rotation, tmp cleanup by a still-running php-fpm request) makes find exit non-zero. The spec does not say whether that is a snapshot-db or reset-files failure.
findings.implementation_impact: A transient vanish fails snapshot-db, or fails reset-files and makes the cell parallel-unconfirmed or sequential-reset, even though the listing is otherwise complete.
findings.suggestion: Specify find ... -print > <tmp> || true, followed by a check that <tmp> is non-empty, or state explicitly that any non-zero find exit is a failure and accept it.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:28 (lockstep barrier) / :91 (.done creation)
findings.issue: Writing a step marker (worker) or creating <engine>.done (version process) can fail with OSError: disk full, dir removed, EACCES. Both waits poll with no timeout and never emit SLOW, and the spec defines no reaction to a failed marker write.
findings.implementation_impact: The other workers wait in barrier-wait forever. The version process waits forever on workers that never exit, so the run hangs silently until --stop-job.
findings.suggestion: Specify that a worker whose step-marker write fails exits without a result (crash), and that a failed .done creation marks every remaining step done for that engine some other way, or kills every worker and records crash cells.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:91 (Worker interface, 'Parseable')
findings.issue: A result counts as parseable when it is a JSON object with the listed keys and the matching engine. The type of result (drive_engine's return), scenario_spans and timings is not constrained, so result: null or non-list scenarios passes the check.
findings.implementation_impact: _fill_cell or the timing re-record raises in the version process on a malformed but 'parseable' result. That crashes the whole version instead of one engine's cell being marked crash.
findings.suggestion: Extend 'parseable' to require that result is an object with a list scenarios, scenario_spans is an object and timings is a list of [str, number, str]. Anything else is crash.

findings.location: Design Notes > Confirmation passes (last sentence: "the contract's 'no further rerun' = no further fallback pass") vs cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7), bullet 3 ("When every engine's login fails, or the second login fails too, BO steps stay inconclusive as today, with no further rerun")
findings.issue: The spec reads a contract sentence differently from its literal text. The Approach declares the contract authoritative for every rule it names. The contract was edited for Budi's two other decisions (slot label, rerun of every engine that drove X), but this sentence still says 'no further rerun'. Read literally, it forbids the `rerun-seq` that the spec runs when every login failed and an engine has FO findings. No I/O row covers 'all logins fail + a finding', so no test pins down which reading wins.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer who follows the authoritative contract skips confirmation in that case, so unconfirmed parallel FO findings block, which breaks the honesty law. One who follows the spec contradicts the contract text. Reviewers and tests can't tell which behaviour is correct.
findings.suggestion: Reword the contract sentence as was done for the other two decisions, e.g. 'no further BO-login fallback pass; an engine with findings still gets its rerun-seq'. Add an I/O row: both logins fail, chromium has FO finding F → `rerun-seq:chromium` runs, F counts only if it reproduces, BO steps stay inconclusive.

findings.location: Design Notes > Logging ("the sequential-mode notice and the BO-login fallback go to stderr and the progress log only"); contract Slots "logs the fallback"
findings.issue: The progress-log format (ps-flashlight-run.py comment above PROGRESS_HEARTBEAT, run-phases.md token table) defines only the tokens START, ALIVE, SLOW, END and DONE, each tied to a phase or to process end. No token or helper writes a free-text notice. The spec doesn't say which token or phase carries these two notices, and the docs task doesn't add a new token to the run-phases.md table.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must invent a token (e.g. `NOTE`), misuse a phase (a zero-length START/END), or skip the progress-log write. An undocumented token breaks operators' and the orchestrator's reading of the log (`_log_has_done` parses column 6). A fake phase would also land in the TimingSink.
findings.suggestion: Name the mechanism explicitly, e.g. a new token `NOTE <phase-less detail>` written via `fl.progress('NOTE', '', text)`, and add it to the run-phases.md token table with 'informational, never stuck'. Or state that the BO-login fallback is visible only as the `browser:<engine>#2` START line and the sequential notice only as stderr.

findings.location: Tasks > docs (SKILL.md Lapis 4 visual review: "reads the `screenshots` of the newest line of `<reports>/<module>-e2e-<ver>-<browser>.jsonl`"; run-phases.md "Tinjauan visual" same source)
findings.issue: The new instruction has the orchestrator open cell history files directly. That conflicts with two existing doc rules the spec leaves in place. SKILL.md line 28 says Lapis 4 history file names 'diturunkan skrip, tak diketik' (derived by the script, not typed). run-phases.md > Istilah E2E says 'Hasil run dibaca dari plan cakupan-run berikutnya, tak pernah dari histori' (results are read from the next plan, never from history). No script output exposes per-cell screenshot paths: the stdout line has only `appended`, and `--merge-only`'s report view is written only at wrap-up.
findings.implementation_impact: The docs writer has to either break the 'never type history names / never read history' rules or invent another source. Orchestrator models given both rules will behave inconsistently, either skipping the review or hand-typing paths.
findings.suggestion: Pick one sanctioned source and amend the conflicting sentences: e.g. add a per-cell `screenshots` map (or the screenshot subdir per appended cell) to ps-run-layer's output line, or explicitly carve out 'visual review only: read the newest history line (path from `ps-run-layer.py --help`)' in both SKILL.md and run-phases.md.

findings.location: Design Notes > Snapshot and reset in shell ("`wait-http` (no response fails the routine ...)") vs Design Notes > Confirmation passes ("After the first failed snapshot, health or reset sub-phase ..."; "Snapshot, health and reset failures never enter version-level `errors`") and Always > Reset
findings.issue: The shared routine can fail at `wait-http` (no HTTP response after the reset). The consequence rules list only 'snapshot, health or reset' failures. It is unclear whether a `wait-http` failure counts as a reset sub-phase. Does it (a) give `parallel-unconfirmed` / `sequential-reset`, (b) stop all further resets, (c) stay out of version-level `errors` (on first boot the same failure goes into version `errors`), and (d) use what `errors` entry name (`wait-http: ...`)?
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must guess. Putting it in version-level `errors` (as first boot does) would make every cell of the version inconclusive through derive_state, including already-confirmed ones. That is the opposite of 'never enter version-level errors'.
findings.suggestion: State that any routine failure (health, reset-db, reset-files, reset-opcache, wait-http with no response) is a routine failure with the same consequences, recorded as `<sub-phase>: <reason>` in cell `errors` only (e.g. `wait-http: no response`).

findings.location: Tasks > docs (run-phases.md: "Istilah E2E gains `sequential-reset` and worker `crash` (meaning, infra cause, remediation ...)"; "`parallel-unconfirmed` → sequential next run")
findings.issue: `parallel-unconfirmed` is an inconclusive reason, so it is an infra cause. The existing 'Sebab infra per versi V' flow makes the orchestrator ask Budi to fix the environment, or refuse, before the next run that includes V. Yet only `sequential-reset` and `crash` get a meaning/remediation entry. For `parallel-unconfirmed` the docs task says only that the next run is sequential, with no meaning, cause or remediation (e.g. 'just rerun: it is admitted at cost 1 with a reset between engines; check container health / progress log').
findings.implementation_impact: The orchestrator prompts Budi to 'fix the environment' with no guidance for this reason, or treats it like `no-slots`. The docs writer must invent the remediation text.
findings.suggestion: Add `parallel-unconfirmed` to the Istilah E2E list with the same three parts (meaning, infra cause, remediation: rerun; the next run is forced sequential; check snapshot/reset lines and container health in the progress log).

findings.location: Boundaries > Honesty law ("a degraded rerun (launch error, failed BO login) keeps the state Design Notes > Confirmation merge gives it, never passing gate-grade")
findings.issue: The merge rules don't guarantee the 'never passing gate-grade' claim for a rerun whose BO login fails. Steps like `goto`/`expect_no_fatal` are conclusive without login (SESSION_INDEPENDENT_ACTIONS; per-step rule in contract State). If a module's BO steps are only those, a rerun with `bo_authed` false has no inconclusive steps and no browser_notes, so the merged cell can be `pass` and passing gate-grade.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer either leaves the claim false, so a test written from the Honesty-law sentence fails, or adds an unspecified rule to force it (e.g. a browser_note), which diverges from single-engine behaviour and from 'identical findings'.
findings.suggestion: Weaken the sentence to 'never passing gate-grade unless every step it left unauthenticated is session-independent, exactly as a single-engine run', or state the extra rule explicitly if Budi wants it.

findings.location: Design Notes > Worker interface ("Parseable = a JSON object with those keys ... whatever the exit code" vs "a worker that exits 143 or by a signal while the version process was not stopped is a `crash`")
findings.issue: The two rules overlap. Take a worker that wrote a valid result and then exited 143 or by signal (e.g. stop_job's direct SIGTERM racing the version process's own, or a stray signal during interpreter exit) while the version process was not stopped. The first rule uses its result; the second makes it a crash.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must pick a precedence. Tests for 'parseable whatever the exit code' and 'exit 143 → crash' can't both pass for that input.
findings.suggestion: State the precedence, e.g. 'a parseable result wins whatever the exit code; the 143/signal → crash rule applies only when no parseable result exists'.

findings.location: Design Notes > Worker interface ("`fl.progress_attach(path, version)` (no truncate; never `progress_init`)"; spec.json carries `slow_after`)
findings.issue: The new helper's signature has no `slow_after`, yet spec.json passes `slow_after` to the worker. The only setter of `_PROGRESS['slow_after']` is `progress_init`, which the worker must not call. `progress_init(path, slow_after, truncate=False)` already does a non-truncating attach, so the reason for a separate helper is unclear.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must guess whether `progress_attach` takes `slow_after`, whether the worker pokes `fl._PROGRESS` directly, or whether `slow_after` is ignored. If ignored, the worker's phases use the default threshold even when the operator passed `--slow-after`.
findings.suggestion: Define `progress_attach(path, version, slow_after=None)`, or say that workers call `progress_init(path, slow_after, truncate=False)` plus `progress_version(version)`, and drop the 'never progress_init' wording.

findings.location: Design Notes > Worker interface (result `timings: [[name, seconds, outcome], ...]` "in record order and unsuffixed"); Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py
findings.issue: `TimingSink` stores only suffixed keys in two dicts (`boot_phases`, `phase_durations`). It keeps no ordered list of unsuffixed events, and the spec doesn't say the worker activates a sink (`timing_activate`). The ps-flashlight-run task lists only `CELL_PHASE_PREFIXES` routing and `progress_attach`, so the capability the result file needs is missing.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must add an event log to TimingSink or reconstruct order and unsuffixed names from dict keys (fragile). Without a named API, the unit test for 're-recorded in order so suffixes continue' has no defined seam.
findings.suggestion: Add to the ps-flashlight-run task: 'TimingSink keeps `events` = [(name, seconds, outcome)] in record order; the worker activates a sink and writes `sink.events` as `timings`'.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always bullet 2 (lockstep barrier) / contract Lockstep
findings.issue: The spec doesn't say whether a worker waits at the barrier after its last step, or exits right after writing the last marker. It also doesn't say whether `finished_at` (stamped 'at the end of its `browser:<engine>` phase') includes that final wait.
findings.implementation_impact: This changes whether a trailing `barrier-wait:<engine>` appears in `phase_durations`, what `finished_at` and `wall_clock` mean, and what the unit tests assert about barrier entries and worker timings.
findings.suggestion: State it, e.g. 'no barrier after the last step: the worker writes its last marker and leaves its browser phase'.

findings.location: Design Notes > Confirmation merge ("`parallel_only` = `[]` on every driven cell of a parallel-mode version unless filled above, else `null`") vs Confirmation passes ("A `crash` or `launch_error` engine ... its partial spans do not count as driven")
findings.issue: 'Driven' is used in two senses. ps-plan-layers `_driven` treats a `launch_error` worker as driven, since it recorded `browser:<engine>`. The confirmation rules say a launch_error engine's spans don't count as driven. It is unclear whether a launch_error cell in parallel mode gets `parallel_only: []` or `null`.
findings.implementation_impact: This is a guess about a record field that tests and the aggregate's `e2e_cells` expose.
findings.suggestion: Say explicitly: `[]` for every cell whose worker left a parseable result (launch_error included), `null` for crash, not-run and probe-dropped cells.

findings.location: Acceptance Criteria 2 / Tasks > live test ("(b) and (c) ... fail, naming the counted slots, when admission fell back to sequential"); Verification ("exit 0 and no SKIPPED line")
findings.issue: The host's Docker daemon is shared: other sessions' and orphan containers count toward `psm.slots`. Live (b) and (c) therefore fail whenever fewer than 2 slots per version are free at admission, which is not a code defect. The done criterion 'passes on every default target version' depends on external daemon load and isn't reproducible.
findings.implementation_impact: Whoever implements this can't reliably show AC 2 is met. A red run doesn't separate a CAP-7 bug from a busy daemon, and the fixed rule 'fail, not skip' leaves no clean way to rerun.
findings.suggestion: Either check free slots up front (`daemon_slot_usage`) and print `SKIPPED: <n> slots free, need 2` (and let Verification accept that), or state that AC 2 is judged only on an otherwise idle daemon and the test prints the counted containers before starting.
